text:
I do not know. Only in the spring

of your eyes there reaches me the gloomy news

of God; only on your lips, the caress

of a world in harvest, of a celestial granary.


Are you clean crystal, or a destroying

snowfield? No, I do not know... Of this delight,

I know only its cosmic greed,

the sidereal beating with which I love you.


I do not know whether you are death or life,

whether I touch rose in you, whether I touch star,

whether I call God or you when I call you.


Reed in the water or deaf wounded stone,

I know only that the afternoon is wide and beautiful,

I know only that I am a man and that I love you.

translation.title: Science of Love
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps the sonnet's claimed ignorance and its cosmic account of embodied love.
